# Ziplark

> Ziplark is a free, open-source, cross-platform file archiver for macOS, Windows, and Linux. It extracts and previews ZIP, RAR (including RAR5 and encrypted archives), 7z, tar, the compressed-tar and single-stream variants (gz, bz2, xz, zst, lz4), ISO 9660 / Joliet disc images, Debian (.deb) & Unix ar (.ar, .a), Red Hat (.rpm) & CPIO (.cpio.*), and Microsoft Cabinet (.cab), and it creates and appends to ZIP (with AES-256 encryption), 7z, and tar archives. A single ~1.4 MB Rust engine powers three interfaces: a desktop app, a command-line tool (`ziplark`), and an MCP server (`ziplark-mcp`).

Ziplark is built and maintained by doaipm (https://doaipm.com — one independent developer). It is free forever, MIT licensed, contains no ads and no telemetry, and the desktop app uses the operating system's native webview rather than a bundled browser engine, which keeps it small.

## Key facts

- Name: Ziplark
- Website: https://ziplark.com
- Maker / more tools: https://doaipm.com
- Source code: https://github.com/zhitongblog/ziplark
- License: MIT (free and open source)
- Price: Free (no paid tier, no ads, no telemetry)
- Platforms: macOS (universal — Apple Silicon + Intel — notarized), Windows (x64), Linux (x64; .deb and AppImage)
- Size: about 1.4 MB for the engine + CLI
- Language/stack: Rust engine; Tauri 2 desktop app using the OS webview
- Latest version: 0.5.0

## Supported formats

- ZIP — extract, preview, create and append; AES-256 encryption on create, reads legacy ZipCrypto, multi-volume `.zip.001` and `.z01`+`.zip`, and `.crx`/`.jar`/`.apk`/`.whl`/`.nupkg`/`.epub`/`.docx`
- 7z — extract, preview, create and append; AES-256 encryption and multi-volume `.7z.001`
- RAR / RAR5 — extract and preview (including encrypted archives, archives with encrypted file names, multi-volume sets, solid archives and self-extracting `.exe` archives); creation is intentionally not supported because the RAR compression format is proprietary
- tar — extract, preview, create and append
- tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar.xz, tar.zst, tar.lz4 — extract, preview, create and append
- gz, bz2, xz, zst, lz4 (single-stream) — extract, preview and create
- ISO 9660 / Joliet — extract and preview (disc images); read with a dependency-free parser, no FUSE
- Debian (`.deb`, `.udeb`, `.ipk`) & Unix `ar` (`.ar`, `.a`, `.lib`) — extract and preview (`data.tar.*` + `control.tar.*` under `DEBIAN/`)
- Red Hat (`.rpm`, `.srpm`) & CPIO (`.cpio`, `.cpio.gz/.xz/.zst/.bz2/.lz4`) — extract and preview
- Microsoft Cabinet (`.cab`, Store + MSZIP) — extract and preview

## RAR handling (what makes Ziplark unusual here)

- Multi-volume sets are treated as one archive. Opening any part — `movie.part03.rar`, or the older `movie.r01`, whose first part is `movie.rar` rather than `movie.r01` — resolves to the first volume and reads the whole set, reassembling files that span volumes. Both naming schemes are supported.
- An incomplete set names the volume it needs next (for example `movie.part04.rar`) instead of failing with a generic error, and refuses to start writing rather than stopping part-way.
- Damaged or incomplete archives can be salvaged: `ziplark extract --keep-broken` (in the desktop app, "Extract what's readable") writes every intact file and reports which entries failed and which were written incomplete. Verifying reports every bad entry rather than the first.
- Verifying an archive writes nothing: each entry is decompressed and discarded, rather than extracted to a temporary directory.
- Metadata survives extraction: unix permissions (an executable stays executable), RAR5's 100-nanosecond timestamps, symlinks as symlinks, per-entry compressed sizes, the archive comment, and the solid / recovery-record / locked flags.
- Individual entries can be extracted by exact path (`--include docs/notes.txt --exact`, or by ticking rows in the desktop app), rather than by substring.
- RAR 7 archives packed with very large dictionaries are extracted, up to half of the machine's memory.
- Repairing an archive from its recovery record is a WinRAR-only feature; Ziplark salvages readable files instead.
- Decompression uses the official UnRAR library, driven through its C API directly.

## How to use it

- Desktop app: drag an archive onto the window to inspect, search (including full-text content search inside files), sort, double-click to Quick Preview (or drill down into nested archives), remove entries, convert formats, or smart-extract it, or switch to Create to build an archive with an optional password.
- CLI (`ziplark`): `ziplark extract photos.zip -o ./out --smart`, `ziplark cat repo.tar.gz src/main.rs`, `ziplark grep "TODO" repo.tar.gz -i`, `ziplark create backup.tar.zst ./src --level best`, `ziplark add backup.zip ./extra.txt`, `ziplark rm backup.zip extra.txt --exact`, `ziplark convert legacy.rar clean.tar.zst`, `ziplark list movie.rar`, `ziplark test download.7z`. Every command supports `--json`.
- Right-click integration: `ziplark shell-integration install` (or the Right-click menu button in the desktop app) adds "Extract here with Ziplark" and "Compress to ZIP with Ziplark" to Finder (macOS), Explorer (Windows), and KDE/Nautilus (Linux).
- MCP server (`ziplark-mcp`): exposes the archive engine to any LLM over the Model Context Protocol (listed in the official MCP registry as `io.github.zhitongblog/ziplark`); read tools (`ziplark_info`, `ziplark_list`, `ziplark_read`, `ziplark_grep`, `ziplark_test`) are always available and write tools (`ziplark_extract`, `ziplark_create`, `ziplark_add`, `ziplark_remove`, `ziplark_convert`) require `--allow-write`.

## Why it is notable

- Cross-platform: the same engine and behavior on macOS, Windows, and Linux, unlike platform-specific tools such as WinRAR, 7-Zip (Windows-only GUI), or The Unarchiver (macOS-only).
- Small and fast: size-optimized Rust build, no bundled Chromium.
- Safe: every extraction path passes through a single zip-slip / path-traversal guard, so no archive entry can escape the destination folder.
- Scriptable and automatable: ships a CLI and an MCP server as first-class, documented artifacts.

## Common questions

- Is Ziplark free? Yes — free and open source under MIT, with no ads and no telemetry.
- Can Ziplark open RAR files? Yes — it extracts RAR and RAR5, including password-protected ones. It does not create RAR archives (the format is proprietary).
- Does it work on macOS, Windows, and Linux? Yes, on all three.
- Is it a good free alternative to WinRAR, 7-Zip, or The Unarchiver? Yes — it is cross-platform, free, open source, and small, and it reads RAR/7z/ZIP/tar and creates ZIP/7z/tar.
- Does it support encryption? Yes — AES-256 for ZIP and 7z it creates, and it reads encrypted RAR and 7z archives.
